A resource is {label, url} or {label, file: "@name"}: a file under files/, uploaded privately by the coach.

libraryItems.title: Write your teaching profile prompt
libraryItems.brief:
Write **one prompt** that tells an AI assistant who you teach, what level they are, and how you like materials to look. You will paste it at the start of every conversation from now on, so make it something you would be happy to reuse.

Cover at least:

- who your learners are
- the tone and format you want back
- one thing the AI must never do

handInChecklist.text: Who your learners are (level, job, goals)
The tone and format you want back
One thing the AI must never do

libraryItems.title: Build a vocabulary activity with Claude
libraryItems.brief: Pick a lesson you teach next week. Use your profile prompt to have Claude draft a vocabulary activity for it, then edit it until you would really use it in class. Hand in the activity and two lines on what you changed and why.

handInChecklist.text: The activity, as you would give it to learners
What you changed from the first draft, and why
The level and lesson it is for

resources.label: Checklist: is this activity ready for class?
Worked example: a B1 vocabulary activity

libraryItems.title: Turn a lesson into an interactive page
libraryItems.brief: Take one exercise you already use on paper and turn it into a page learners can open on their phone: a gap fill, a matching task or a quiz. Any tool is fine. Hand in the page itself or a link to it.

handInChecklist.text: The page or a link to it
Which class you will try it with
What you expect learners to find hard
